title: Nvidia Halves DGX Spark Memory in $4,999 Oct 23 Launch
summary:
The semiconductor giant will release a 64GB DGX Spark workstation that can handle local AI models of up to 100B parameters. The system launches on Oct. 23 with a starting price of $4,999 through partners including Acer, ASUS, Dell, Gigabyte, HP, and MSI. Utilizing the GB10 Grace Blackwell chip, the units can be linked over 200GbE via Nvidia Sync to pool 128GB of memory, permitting the use of 200B parameter models and delivering up to 1.7x the performance of a single system.

Market observers noted the hardware reduces memory in half compared to the previous 128GB version while maintaining a similar street price. This transition to lower memory specifications coincides with a forecast from Micron that memory supply will remain tight through 2028, a condition some analysts suggest has increased pricing power for hardware providers.

NVIDIA $NVDA is launching a new 64GB DGX Spark on Oct. 23, starting at $4,999 through Acer, ASUS, Dell, Gigabyte, HP and MSI.

It keeps the GB10 Grace Blackwell chip and supports models up to 100B parameters locally.

Two units can be linked over 200GbE to pool 128GB of memory and run models up to 200B parameters, with NVIDIA reporting up to 1.7x performance vs. one system.

NVIDIA Sync will automatically configure the two-system cluster.
